correctness.rationale: Centered roots from two perfect matchings are complementary (k-1)-simplices, with only their individual zero-sum relations, so free-sum facets omit one from each; count k² and intrinsic dim 2k-2. Solving exact facet normal equations gives x_h=-d+k1_{1<=((h-i) mod k)<=d} and y_h=x_h-1+k1_{h=i}; ||n_ij||²=k[k-1+2d(k-1-d)] and support value 1. Maximizing d(k-1-d) gives stated radius for both parities and k or 2k contacts. Cyclic center-averaging proves optimality; zero-sum contacting normals force active equalities at any optimum. For odd k, their span rank k-1; for even k the differences of adjacent contacting offset normals span ker(x-y), rank 2k-2, proving unique center. Independently reconstructed exact normals, Gram norms and rank for k=2..7; finite checks only diagnostics.
